rounds.text: Adhata Global Ltd displays clear evidence of an operational turnaround that the market has not fully recognized, led by recent YoY sales expansion of 112%, sequential QoQ sales growth, and net profit growth of 18% YoY [E48] [E51] [E50]. This operational acceleration is further highlighted by quarterly operating margins expanding by 119 percentage points YoY in Sep 2026 [E25] alongside a strong results score of 90/100, which indicates fundamental improvement while price sentiment remains cautious [E53]. Management has also systematically derisked the business by reducing borrowings from Rs 2.20 Cr down to Rs 0.71 Cr in Sep 2026 [E32] [E40], supported by high insider alignment with 75.00% promoter ownership [E34] and a long-term 10-year compounded sales growth rate of 19% [E13]. Conceded: [E16] and [E18], trailing twelve-month figures remain heavily burdened by historical contraction with sales down 65% and profit down 603%, driving return on equity to -87.65% [E8] and return on capital employed to -47.28% [E9]. However, with the stock hovering at 0% of its 52-week range [E4], current valuation reflects past weakness rather than the emerging operational recovery [E53].

Adhata Global Ltd exhibits severe fundamental deterioration, evidenced by a collapsing top-line where compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months stands at -65% [E16] and poor five-year sales growth of -29% [E14], alongside a compounded profit growth collapse of -603% in the TTM [E18]. This operational bleed translates into catastrophic profitability metrics, featuring a trailing twelve-month ROE of -87.65% [E8] and an operating margin of -62% that has degraded by 50 percentage points over three years [E24]. Furthermore, the company suffers from extreme working capital strains, highlighted by exceptionally high debtors of 497 days [E45] and negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -1.41 Cr and Rs -1.42 Cr respectively for March 2026 [E29, E30]. Despite these severe operational losses and cash burn, the stock trades at an unjustifiable price-to-book multiple of 5.21x against a book value of ₹ 3.80 [E1], sitting at the very bottom of its 52-week range at 0% [E4], while promoter holdings have simultaneously drifted downward to 75.00% [E34]. Conceded: quarterly operating margins showed a relative improvement in September 2026 [E25] and the company has managed to reduce its debt borrowings down to Rs 0.71 Cr [E32].

Conceded: trailing twelve-month sales and profit growth metrics show steep declines [E16, E18], and operating cash flow for March 2026 is negative [E29]. However, the bear overlooks a powerful operational turnaround already underway: quarterly operating margins surged by 119 percentage points in September 2026 compared to the year-ago period [E25], and recent results score a high 90 out of 100 with accelerating net profit growth up 18% year-on-year [E50, E53]. Furthermore, the company has successfully slashed its debt borrowings down to Rs 0.71 Cr from Rs 2.20 Cr a year earlier [E32], directly countering concerns over financial obligations. Conceded: debtors stand at an elevated 497 days [E45], yet the rules-based screening and bias checklist explicitly warn against dismissing this active operational recovery based on stale, backward-looking sentiment [E47, E53]. Finally, long-term historical records demonstrate the business's capacity for strong expansion, evidenced by a 19% compounded sales growth rate over a 10-year span [E13].

Conceded: quarterly operating margins improved by 119 percentage points in September 2026 compared to the year-ago period [E25], and net profit grew 18% year-on-year [E50]. However, this supposed turnaround sits against a severe collapse in trailing twelve-month growth, where sales dropped 65% and profit growth plummeted 603% [E16, E18]. The bull points to debt reduction down to Rs 0.71 Cr [E32], but ignores that the company still suffers from a low interest coverage ratio, high borrowing costs, and negative operating and free cash flows of Rs -1.41 Cr and Rs -1.42 Cr respectively for March 2026 [E29, E30, E42, E46]. Furthermore, the bull minimizes the alarming 497-day debtor burden [E45] and deeply negative return metrics, including an ROE of -79.4% and an ROE of -87.65% against a sector benchmark of 8.89% [E8, E12]. Dismissing these persistent structural risks as stale sentiment ignores that the stock trades at an unjustifiable price-to-book ratio of 5.21x to 5.22x while sitting at the absolute bottom of its 52-week range at 0% of the span [E1, E4, E6].
